newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bavaria minister - EMU could start without France.
newsitem.headline: Bavaria minister - EMU could start without France.

text.p: European monetary union (EMU) could start without France if that country does not meet the entry criteria, the finance minister of conservative Bavaria said.

"If France fails to meet the 3.0 percent (budget deficit to GDP) criterion this year, Paris cannot belong to the circle of participants until it meets the criterion," Erwin Huber told the news magazine Focus.
"It is thoroughly conceivable that EMU will start without France," Huber said.
No country, not even a founding member of the European Union, has a free pass to join EMU, Huber said. The interview, due to be published on Monday, was released in advance.
The 3.0 percent hurdle is not just for Germany, it is for all countries that hope to join EMU, he said.

Huber was responding to comments by French finance minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn that France's deficit will be above three percent of GDP this year, which is the key year for deciding the starting EMU participants.

Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber, a hardline advocate of a strict interpretation of the EMU targets, recently won a pledge from Chancellor Helmut Kohl that the 3.0 percent rule should be firmly applied.
